name: NLC India Ltd
tagline: Navratna PSU lignite-miner-cum-thermal-power generator explicitly reshaping itself into a diversified renewable-energy player (10 GW target by 2030, green hydrogen/BESS/pumped-storage optionality, a stated green-arm IPO plan) - a genuine, named capital-allocation regime change, but at ~Rs 37,400 Cr and flat revenue, size alone rules out an extreme-return thesis.
business_overview: NLC India Ltd (formerly Neyveli Lignite Corporation) mines lignite and operates thermal power plants, and is now explicitly pivoting toward renewables: a stated corporate target of 10 GW+ renewable capacity by 2030 (from 734 MW operational plus ~5.81 GW under implementation/development, ~2.5 GW under construction), aiming for a ~50:50 conventional/green asset balance, with additional optionality in green hydrogen, battery energy storage, pumped-storage hydro, lignite-to-methanol and a reported plan to IPO its green-energy arm. Confirmed as the exact listed entity matching state.json name via screener.in/tickertape (NSE: NLCINDIA). Seeded via untrusted X triage (@StocksResearch, 2026-09-13, high conviction).
fundamentals_table: 10 GW+ by 2030 (734 MW operational + ~5.81 GW pipeline, ~2.5 GW under construction)
fundamentals_narrative: Core lignite/thermal revenue is flat (~-0.3%) and returns are modest (ROCE ~7.7%, ROE ~11-15%) for a PSU carrying D/E ~1.1 - the legacy business alone would not clear this project's bar. What changes the picture is a concrete, already-under-construction renewable build-out (2.5 GW under construction today, 10 GW targeted by 2030, roughly matching the existing thermal fleet) plus real optionality in green hydrogen, BESS and pumped storage, and a reported plan to eventually list the green-energy arm separately - a genuine capital-allocation regime change, not just aspirational language. Valuation remains undemanding (P/E ~10.6x, P/B ~1.7x).
